title: Ride-along to assess 4 frontier models' proficiency at discrete stock analysis and picking tasks (Astra, Fable, Gemini, Grok)
author: Frodo_Baghodler
selftext:
I'm building an AI stock trader. It will be paper trading using its own research, risk analysis, and decision making. I'm going to be using all 4 models in a single conversation as we go along to check each others' work and see how proficient each model is at individual tasks. I'll call it out as the different models screw up along the way. Input welcome! I want to put them through their paces.

Stage 0: Screener

Screened 680 stocks into a candidate pool of 42.

Screenshot shows how each did but here's a summary:

\- Grok 4.6 XHigh screwed the pooch and didn't even follow its own gates reliably.

\- Gemini 3.8 Flash High failed at counting and attributing findings.

\- Claude Fable 5.1 Max failed to find info that was available online in 3 different places. 

\- GPT-6 Astra Max did virtually perfectly.

comments.author: QuanTradin
comments.body:
Running them in a single conversation means every model after the first can see the earlier answers. That isn't four independent attempts, it's one attempt and three reviews, and it will make the later ones look better than they are. Worth running stage 0 cold in four separate sessions and only then putting them in a room together.

Stage 0 is also mostly an instruction following test rather than a stock analysis one. Still useful to know, just a different question from the one you're asking.

replies.author: Frodo_Baghodler
replies.body: Yes, you're correct but I should note that they're prompted to attempt the task independently first before comparing their results to the previous models' output. You're right that the sneaky AI could still peak but I let that slide for a few reasons: I need to come to a single best answer to develop an actual paper trading portfolio that I'll be testing, I didn't want to rely on a single model for fact checking at the end, and because it's faster and easier than the more scientific approach you recommended, and I think I'll still get 90% of the insight into the models' performance.

replies.author: QuanTradin
replies.body: Makes sense for what you're optimising for. The bit I'd flag is that once a model has seen the others' output you've stopped measuring four models and started measuring one ensemble with extra steps. Fine if the ensemble is the product, awkward if you wanted a per model ranking out of it.
